report.explanation:
Reviewer B — E06-only round 1/5. Source verdict: FAIL.

Scoring: total_items=2 actionable findings; must_fix=[]; should_fix=[B-01, B-02]; consider=[]. Score=100×(2−0−2)/2=0%; the required ≥94% threshold is not met. These findings concern introduced source defects, not the separately outstanding live-acceptance prerequisite.

Should-fix findings:
• B-01 — P2 — src/tui.rs:794–796: Recovery compares the captured target tuple strictly before allowing initial session establishment. If a starting view was captured with session_id:null and the original agent completes session/new during disconnection/pause, recovery permanently displays Ended for that still-surviving instance. Evidence: attached() validates at line913 before normal-loop null-to-established-session handling at lines1044–1050 and1174–1182; daemon ACP open returns a starting/null-session target, and ACP NewSession processing assigns its first session without replacing the instance. Apply the same bounded initial-establishment rule on recovery while preserving daemon/view/instance/connection identity checks and rejecting changes to established sessions.
• B-02 — P2 — src/tui.rs:1063–1070: After receiving a successful launch receipt, the client selects the launched ID but does not update Resume until a subsequent observation snapshot succeeds. Transport failure on that read leaves recovery bound to the previous view—or the empty initial CLI-start target—so the client reconnects to the wrong prior view or incorrectly reports Ended while the acknowledged new agent survives. Evidence: supervise() retries using Resume, and attached() chooses Resume.active; the exact newly launched tuple is already available in opened.target. Persist that continuity record before the fallible follow-up snapshot, without replaying the launch.

Seven review dimensions:
1. Correctness: Traced CLI/picker launch through daemon profile resolution and broker reservation, configuration RPC production through Configure reply dispatch and readiness admission, peer cancellation through original responder/writer completion, and recovery through supervision. B-01/B-02 prevent an unconditional correctness PASS.
2. Conventions: Configuration remains on disk and runtime identities/work remain memory-only; stock terminal routes remain distinct from ACP; closed inputs and explicit errors are retained. No additional actionable convention violation identified.
3. Behavior tests: New tests assert observable effects, original identities, rejected settings, same-process continuation, ownership, no replay, and cleanup rather than source wiring. Force negative cases remain meaningful, and canonical-render fencing improves question navigation. Recovery tests establish ready agents before attachment and omit the startup-session and acknowledged-launch/failed-snapshot boundaries behind these findings.
4. Design: Concrete profiles, settings state, launch dialog, and owned NativeControl worker reuse existing boundaries without a second protocol or generic plugin layer. No separate design blocker identified.
5. Edge cases: Examined missing/unavailable profiles, ambiguous project names, bounded/unsupported/conflicting settings, typed cancellation IDs and admitted winners, opaque tool IDs, socket loss, paused clients, missing targets, and replacement daemons. The two reported gaps are launch/recovery boundary cases.
6. Security: Reviewed capability/generation admission, exact permission responders, shell-free argv, metadata sanitization, fresh recovery provenance, and shutdown/join handling. No additional evidence-backed introduced security finding identified; trusted same-user configuration and historical native-settlement limitations are excluded.
7. Refactoring/Fowler smells: Duplicated Code in normal-loop first-session reconciliation contributes to B-01 by excluding recovered entry. No independent actionable Mysterious Name, Feature Envy, Data Clumps, Primitive Obsession, Message Chains, or Middle Man finding identified.

Acceptance remains separate: Parent-reported mechanical/offline/controlling-PTY successes do not turn the failing full live task into PASS. Eight of nine approved actual requests were consumed, one remains unused, and no additional live execution is authorized. Physical suspend, Linux, and minimum-toolchain execution remain unexercised as stated in the brief.

I performed read-only source/diff/spec review only. I did not edit files, execute builds/tests/linters/formatters/smokes/providers/auth flows, inspect private runtime/auth/database/session/log fixtures, or read another current reviewer report.
